title: Business eligibility and ownership guidelines
measures: Eligibility rule that a business must make in-person contact with customers during stated hours; ineligible business types; rules for owners and authorized representatives (agencies), including transferring ownership to the business owner on request and that website content must be owned and managed by the business owner.
limitations: Policy page; Google may change it without notice. No last-updated date shown.

title: Add a business opening date
measures: A business that has not opened can create a profile and set an opening date up to one year ahead; after verification the profile shows 90 days before the opening date; reviews and user edits are not possible until the business is officially open; a 'Recently opened' tag shows for 90 days after opening.
limitations: Feature behaviour may change; does not describe verification method requirements.

title: Verify your business with a video recording
measures: What a verification video must show for storefront businesses: location context, permanent signage matching the profile name, and proof of management; live, unedited recording of at least 30 seconds; no other people's faces or private information.
limitations: Google chooses which verification methods are offered to a given profile; video is only one of them.

title: About access levels in your Google Ads account
measures: Access levels (Email-only, Billing, Read-only, Standard, Admin) and what each can do; advice to keep more than one admin; linked manager accounts with ownership can edit user access.
limitations: Interface and level names may change.

title: Manager Accounts (MCC): About ownership of client accounts
measures: A client account can have only one owner manager account; a manager that creates an account becomes its owner automatically; linked existing accounts are not owned unless the client enables it; the client account retains its data and can remove ownership access.
limitations: Describes Google's product mechanics, not contract terms between a practice and an agency.

title: Access and data-restriction management
measures: GA4 roles: Administrator has full control including user management; Editor has full control of settings but cannot manage users; roles inherit from account to property.
limitations: Role names and permissions may change.

title: Managing owners, users, and permissions
measures: Verified owners, delegated owners, full users and restricted users in Search Console; a property needs at least one verified owner.

title: Registrants' Benefits and Responsibilities
measures: Registrant rights to review the registration agreement and to information about transfer and renewal processes; registrant responsibility for accurate contact data and for responding to registrar inquiries.
limitations: Applies to ICANN-accredited registrars; country-code domains may follow other rules.

title: About Target ROAS bidding
measures: Definition of ROAS as conversion value divided by ad spend times 100%; eligibility requirement of conversions with valid values; note that a target that is too high may limit traffic.
limitations: Uses an ecommerce example; conversion value is whatever the advertiser reports, not necessarily collected revenue or profit.

title: About conversion values
measures: How advertisers assign the same or different values to conversions and use the Conversion value/cost column to judge return.
limitations: Values are advertiser-supplied; accuracy depends on the business's own data.

title: About offline conversion imports
measures: Importing offline outcomes (for example sales that happen at an office or by phone) back to Google Ads; enhanced conversions for leads as the recommended starting point; notice of a June 15, 2026 migration of API uploads to the Data Manager API.
limitations: Mechanics only. Any upload of patient-related data needs the practice's own privacy and legal review.

title: Get started with attribution
measures: Attribution as the assignment of credit for key events across touchpoints; available models (data-driven, paid and organic last click, Google paid channels last click); direct visits excluded from credit unless the whole path is direct.
limitations: Covers website/app behaviour Analytics can observe, not phone calls or in-office outcomes unless imported.

title: 16 CFR Part 255 — Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising
measures: Section 255.2(b): an endorsement describing a consumer's experience is likely to be read as representative of what consumers generally achieve; without substantiation, the ad should clearly and conspicuously disclose generally expected performance.
limitations: FTC guides interpret Section 5 of the FTC Act; they are not themselves binding regulations. Application to agency case studies should be checked with counsel.

title: 16 CFR Part 465 — Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials
measures: Section 465.2 prohibits businesses from writing, creating, selling or knowingly disseminating consumer reviews or testimonials that misrepresent that the reviewer exists, used the product or service, or the reviewer's experience.
limitations: Federal rule text; enforcement and interpretation are for the FTC and courts.

title: Target ads to geographic locations
measures: Difference between Presence and Presence or Interest location options, and when Google suggests Presence targeting (reaching only users in specific locations).
limitations: Google recommends broad targeting as a default; local service businesses must judge which option fits their catchment.
